subject: Re: POC trial — model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@acmehealth.com>; Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: POC trial next steps and model selection

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and clear priorities on your side. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial: 

Summary of needs
- Primary goal: Automate clinical intake summarization + triage to appropriate care teams.
- Success criteria: 90%+ correctness on triage labels (per your internal eval set), average summary ROUGE-L >= 0.55, and end-to-end inference latency < 350ms p50 on a typical 1-2k token prompt.
- Multilingual requirement: English + Spanish; potential Spanish medical notes with occasional code-switching.

Proposed POC scope (high level)
1) 2-week sandbox trial with 1 sample production route (ingest -> summarize -> triage)
2) Provide model candidates: Llama 2 13B quantized (default) + fallback Mistral 7B; optional instruction-tuned multilingual variant for Spanish tests.
3) Deliverables: sandbox endpoint, evaluation harness (we'll run your labeled set), weekly checkpoint calls.

Ownership & timeline
- Acme: provide labeled eval set (ideally 300-500 representative notes) and a sample traffic recipe by 7/24.
- Redwood: provision sandbox, baseline model config, and run initial eval by 7/30.

Attachments: POC scope and tentative evaluation criteria attached.

Next steps
- Sophie: confirm acceptance of the success criteria above and timeline.
- Tom: share the eval dataset link or password-protected upload location.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa in to coordinate infra and Aditya for model runtime tuning.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_poc_scope.pdf (PDF)]
From: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC trial next steps and model selection

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the triage label target is fine; for ROUGE-L, we care more about clinical fidelity than raw ROUGE, so please include a manual review bucket (10% of eval) to validate critical errors.
- Latency: 350ms p50 is acceptable; p95 should be < 900ms if possible.
- Spanish: we have ~120 Spanish notes in the dataset; many include medical abbreviations. If you can evaluate a Spanish instruction-tuned variant that would be helpful.

We’ll upload the eval set by Friday (7/24). I’ll send an S3 link to Tom and Ben.

One ask: can Redwood recommend a fallback model that is cheaper for bursty traffic, even if accuracy drops slightly?

Appreciate it — Sophie
Sophie Nguyen
Head of Product, Acme Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC trial next steps and model selection

Sophie — thanks, great notes. Quick responses inline and an updated model plan: 

- Manual review: noted. We’ll reserve a 10% manual review sample and create a reviewer spreadsheet for your team.
- Latency targets: we’ll aim for p50 < 350ms and p95 < 900ms in the sandbox; if we can’t meet p95 on the larger context, we’ll look at prefix caching and sequence truncation heuristics.
- Spanish: we’ll include an instruction-tuned multilingual candidate. Our recommended model slate for the trial: 
  * Primary candidate: Llama 2 13B (int8 quantized) — good accuracy/latency balance and strong instruction following.
  * Multilingual candidate: Mistral-instr-13B-multi (instruction-tuned multilingual checkpoint) — for Spanish-heavy tests.
  * Fallback (cost-optimized): Mistral 7B quantized — significantly cheaper for bursty fallback; we’ll also configure automatic routing so lower-tier requests go to the fallback during high load.

Evaluation plan (what Redwood will run)
- Run your labeled set through each candidate and provide per-class precision/recall, ROUGE-L, latency histograms, and a manual error breakdown for the 10% sample.
- We’ll provide a short dashboard and a downloadable CSV with predictions.

Operational notes
- We’ll set up model variants and an automatic fallback policy in the sandbox. You can toggle routing in the Redwood Console or we'll set an initial policy (route 100% to primary; on CPU/GPU shortage, fall back to Mistral 7B).
- Tokens/cost: we’ll estimate per-request cost after the initial eval and propose a cost-optimized quantization profile if needed.

Next steps / owners
- Acme (Sophie/Tom): upload eval set by 7/24 + sample traffic pattern
- Redwood (Marissa): provision sandbox + run initial eval by 7/30
- Redwood (Aditya): set up model configs and quantization profiles; initial tuning on Spanish examples

Attachments: updated eval criteria file.

I’ll schedule a 30-min checkpoint for Thursday (7/23) — Marissa, can you propose times?

Best,
Ben
[Attachment: model_eval_criteria.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme POC — model slate & immediate actions (do not forward)

Marissa / Aditya —

Quick internal note after the Acme call. Please action the items below so we meet the 7/30 evaluation deadline: 

Action items
- Marissa: provision sandbox (GPU-backed) with routing rules. Create a workspace and share credentials with Sophie. Confirm ETA by end of day 7/23.
- Aditya: prepare three model configs: Llama2-13b-int8, mistral-instr-13b-multi, mistral-7b-int8. Include default quantization settings and a Spanish tokenizer test. Run a quick smoke test on a small Spanish set (Aditya, please forward results).
- Ben: I’ll coordinate dataset intake and HubSpot updates; I’ll also confirm the 30-min checkpoint time once Marissa posts availability.

Notes: prioritize the multilingual tokenizer checks — Acme’s Spanish notes have a lot of abbreviations. Also flag any license constraints for the instruction-tuned multilingual checkpoint (if any).

Thanks,
Ben
